text:
Shane Pinto turned 26 on November 12 and celebrated by scoring twice against Colorado, including the overtime winner. It fit the month: 7 goals in his last 10 games, 9 goals and 17 points in 21 overall, playing just over 20 minutes a night as Ottawa's middle-six center. TSN's Frankie Corrado said on air that Pinto "looks like he's ready to break out as a 2nd line centre," and the role is clearly his to lose.

Some of this will cool. He's scoring on 23.1% of his shots against a league norm of 13.3%, and his 9 goals come from 7.21 expected goals, the quality of the chances he's had. Over his last ten games, 7 goals came from 3.9 expected. The shot volume is light, 39 shots in 21 games.

What holds up is the context: he's still getting to good ice (1.02 expected goals per hour, close to last season's 1.16), he's a big-minutes, dangerous-ice shooter in the Tom Wilson and Nico Hischier mold, and he's 13th in the league in wins added by his goals. Watch whether the shots climb as the finishing settles.
headline: Shane Pinto is making the second-line case
